text_fidelity_a: Polar Verity Sense - Optical Heart Rate Monitor Armband for Sport - ANT+ and Dual Bluetooth HRM - Waterproof HR Sensor with only One Button - Compatible with Peloton, Zwift and other apps, Gray, M-XXL I bought this specifically because it's supposed to work with the FORM swim goggles. Unfortunately, it does not. At least not for me. The goggles are quite wide. So, when I attached the HR monitor to my goggle strap as instructed, it was on the outside of my swim cap! So, I had to wear my goggles under my cap. Not great for my hair, but not the end of the world. During the first swim, the HR would disconnect from the goggles as soon as my face was in the water! OK. The next swim, I tightened the straps. Nope. That wasn't it. So, the next swim, I switched caps to a cap that I don't wear as it's too tight. But I thought maybe it would help. Nope! The connection STILL dropped as soon as my face was in the water. After exporting the FORM .fit file and importing it into GarminConnect (my preferred system of tracking my swim/bike/run workouts), I could see that the connection was definitely dropping. I tried everything I could think of to get it stayed connected, but sadly, it just wouldn't. VERY disappointed. Hopefully, FORM will figure out how to connect with GARMIN devices, like the 945 I wear on my wrist! It has an optical HR monitor. Unfortunately, since FORM hasn't done a deal with Garmin, I have to use it at the same time I'm using the FORM goggles but view the HR data AFTER I'm done swimming. :-(  I love Garmin and their customer support has been AMAZING! I've been using their products for 15 years. This is my first Polar product. I'll be returning it.

GREAT. Put a throw rug on your floor for bounce back so your wood or vinyl isn't damaged. Yes.....you really can miss the whole entire board. YOOHO 4 Piece Kayak Paddles for Adult with Comfort Grips Adjuatable Kayak Oars for Easy to Carry and Store Perfect for Kayaking Boating 91.8in/230cm Aluminum Shaft PP Blade My wife and I enjoy kayaking and she enjoys SUPing - my ankles are not strong enough and while I do it, I tend to end up sitting longer than standing. To that end I grabbed these YOOHO Kayak Paddle with Comfort Grips 4 Piece Adjuatable Paddles to take instead of a SUP paddle with my new SUP. A couple things: 1. we have done both kayaking and SUPing, but always in a group, so we are new at having our own and beginners with limited knowledge of what is good vs. not. This is all presented from that beginners perspective. 2. While we have new SUPs and paddles, we are not able to get out for several more weeks. Between a very rainy year so far in 2021 and my recent major surgery limiting what I can do, we are getting these as a promise to ourselves and with an eye to being back out and active as soon as possible. Therefore, this review is also from having and using the paddle out of the water.

Having read about paddles and having used them in a limited way, I do find that these YOOHO Kayak Paddle with Comfort Grips 4 Piece Adjuatable Paddles are a big heavier - I’ve held lighter. But it’s fine for my needs. We will get out there several times a year on salt water (mostly intercostal) and we feel this will be a good set for the setting and our ability level. It looks nice - I like the blue and black - and the materials seem solid. That said, I cannot give this a 5 star rating - it only deserves 4 stars in that putting it together - while easy - was hindered by a peg that was/is not exactly spot on. As you can see in the pics, one button went in well - easy on the first try - on both ends. The other one does not. I tried it first actually, placing it in, getting it lined up, but it is JUST-THAT-OFF (short) that it would not pop out. I tried the other end. It also did not pop out. As I am recovering from surgery I was not able to “fight it’ and had my wife. She was finally - after much effort - able to fight in into one end where it would pop out securing it into place by the pop out. Because of this 1. It’s far harder to set in place that is should and 2. makes us question it’s strength when in use. Would it too easily pop out? So to that end, 4 stars. They need to do better on lining up those pegs that keep the ends in place. It seems like a great paddle, but it needs to get together and apart quickly, easily, and stay together safely. This YOOHO Kayak Paddle with Comfort Grips 4 Piece Adjuatable Paddle set is not good enough to say it does that.
text_fidelity_b: YOOHO 4 Piece Kayak Paddles for Adult with Comfort Grips Adjuatable Kayak Oars for Easy to Carry and Store Perfect for Kayaking Boating 91.8in/230cm Aluminum Shaft PP Blade

text_fidelity_a:
SOG Specialty Knives & Tools SV68 Vision I purchased this knife because I am getting tired of carrying around my Tomcat 3.0 in a sheath. A big selling point for me was the pocket clip of the new model Vision, the knife being all metal, and the VG-10 steel blade. If I had received the older model, well I would have had to return it. The knife arrived with a razor sharp blade right out of the box.

This knife took some getting used to compared to the Tomcat. The Vision is much thinner than the Tomcat in regards to the whole knife. The Tanto blade has additional unique grind lines. I believe SOG did this so that the knife blade being only .125 thick would have the strength of a knife of .150 - .160 thick when it comes to possibly breaking the knife tip.

It appears to me that SOG invested much into the knife being very thin, convenient to carry, and a very large blade for how small the knife is. That is exactly what I needed, I always have a knife with me. It is a little more difficult to handle compared to the Tomcat due to the thinness of the knife.

With the thinness of the Vision, it still seems very strong. There was no sacrifice in strength with this design. I love the handle. I wish SOG offered the same type of handle with more of their knives.

After playing around with my new Vision, until my thumb bled LOL! (that is expected with any new knife for me), then going back to the Tomcat, now my Tomcat feels big and bulky. For a sheath knife and heavy use, I do like the Tomcat better. For convenience to carry, and personal protection, I think I like the Vision better.

The Vision is a great knife, it has a very unique heavy duty thin feel to it.

Would definitely recommend. A word of caution to those with large hands. It may be difficult to get used to.

Sincerely,

10Wolf
text_fidelity_b: SOG Specialty Knives & Tools SV68 Vision

text_fidelity_a:
Mazama Intake Water Bladder | Easy to Fill and Leak Proof | Replacement for Hydration Reservoir for Backpacks and Day Packs I have other Mazama water bladders, and really wanted to like this. I bought it for a trip to the national parks in UT where you should be carrying more water. The good is that its a big reservoir, and the hose is thicker so the rate of flow is higher than their other hoses. What I love about Mazama is the magnetic holder for the hose, and this one is even better because there is some play in it where as the normal version can pop off at times (I generally wear it while mountain biking and its fine, but if there isn't enough slack in the hose it will pop off the magnet).

What I don't like about this one...the closure for the bladder is not secure. I found out by dumping about two liters of water over me when it was in my backpack and I bent forward. I know it looks like it should work, but because its plastic and malleable there is play there and its not perfect. The "lock" wiggles even without pressure, so its suspect to begin with. The way it opens is nice for cleaning, drying, and filling, and the "spine" is helpful for carrying and moving it around. These features cannot make up for the closure however, and I worry about it whenever the bladder is full. I'm also not a fan of the way the bite valve works...it can be left full open and water will just run out, or you can get it to work if you bite a little...but just a little because if you bit too much the rubber tip falls off. Squirely bugger.

When using in the future I might add a clamp or something to ensure the closure can't slip off, and will use my other hose vs this one.
text_fidelity_b: Mazama Intake Water Bladder | Easy to Fill and Leak Proof | Replacement for Hydration Reservoir for Backpacks and Day Packs

A Mustard Seed Toys Tungsten Putty Weight, 1 oz, Get The Perfect Weights for Your Pinewood Car to Win Your Derby I've been working on pinewood derby cars for a while. I first started with my children, then the past 10 years holding derby car clinics.

Tungsten putty is important to get your car to maximum weight. I keep the unassembled car weighted at 4.9 ounces. I drill a shallow 1/4 hole under the car and pack in the tungsten putty to make up the last bit of weight. That way on race day you can make small weight adjustments without trashing your car. The fastest car is the heaviest.

I've been getting tungsten putty from the large online derby suppliers. I figured I'd save money in shipping, use Amazon prime, and try a new product. This putty is less dense than the putty I've worked with in the past. It seems to have more sticky binder and less tungsten powder than what I've used in the past. I ordered 3 units. They easily fit inside one container. I even mixed some tungsten powder to the 3 blobs of putty.

I prefer the stuff I got before but this will work

We now consider these unusable and are looking for better quality products.

You might be able to limp them along if you are willing to sync them with your mobile device daily/near-daily as this refreshes the data (like the time and alarms, etc). However I find the mobile app/syncing process to be tiresome - it's slow, it doesn't always save settings (the watch face is the worst offender, it changes itself seemingly at will), sometimes it takes multiple attempts to connect. I had purchased this product as it was one of the only ones which offered a "family account" and I have 2 children so I did not want to have to install the same app twice. But I still have to, essentially, "log out" of one child's settings and then sync to the other's in order to do anything like change alarms. I often wish I could make all the changes whenever it's convenient and then sync them to push those changes at a later time.

We bought this item as a test run to see if our kids would enjoy using a smartwatch enough to justify investing in decent ones. I would not recommend this item if you intend to use it long-term - save yourself the money and buy a better quality device.

text_fidelity_a:
Srynriwim Collapsible Stool, 2022 Upgraded Portable Folding Stool Lightweight and Sturdy, Indoor Telescopic Stool Non-Slip, Waterproof Camping Stool for Outdoor Fishing Hiking Gardening BBQ(Blue) A bit of a conumdrum here with two ways to look at it. I am 6'3" and currently weigh 225 Lbs. Not a lightweight but as my Pulmonologist informs me "you're no longer clinically obese, you're just obese". Thanks Doc! A left-handed compliment if I ever heard one.

And there lies the rub. The first time I shook this out I had mild difficulty in getting the tabs and latches to hook up-- like I did just now. That seems to inspire a little less confidence in how safely it will support me without crashing down. Once it is expanded and set up it appears to be pretty sturdy. The color also makes it easy to see in the yard.

But having just had double knee replacement I was a bit concerned that it would hold me without making me faceplant in the yard. When I asked my wife to watch me sit on it in the kitchen she said "don't do that!". The sight of me pulling it out and clicking it together didn't inspire confidence in her either.

It did hold me while sitting still although I was a bit reluctant to shift my weight around on it. That would be my major sticking point. On a yard that is not completely level I know that I would have to be careful. The other part of that is that leaning forward or to one side suddenly puts additional stress on whichever part of the base is sitting on the ground. I am not convinced that leaning over wouldn't cause the stool to buckle and me to fall over.

text_fidelity_a:
Black Diamond Spot Headlamp My favorite low priced headlamp.
Not the quality of high tech wonder lamps. But there are no real faults. And the interface is very good.
All inputs on one button which is the best way to do it, fewer moving parts to go wrong.
3 inputs : momentary push, 3 second push, 6 second push.
If the lamp is on :
Momentary push cycles on/off.
Long push gradually dims the light in steps.
(when it reaches the dimmest it will flicker once to indicate lowest level,
then it gradually brightens the light, step at a time, flickers once on highest).
This works very well to set the brightness levels.

When light is OFF:
momentary push turns it on (two outer lights for flood, or center for spot. Repeat pushes will alternate: spot, off, flood, off, spot,...
3 second push : turns on the red lamp
6 second push: turns on the lock mode (locks lamp off until another 6 sec. push turns it back on. A blue light on the side will go on for a couple seconds to verify the lamp is locked).

I find the interface easy to use to get it to do as I like when I like.
5 different tilt settings from straight down to higher than straight forward. There are settings I find perfect for reading or watching your step on the trail. And they stay put.

Very bright on spot!
The flood is very spread out, lights up the whole room or tent.

5 stars.
------

Another lamp that costs about $10 more is the Princeton Tec EOS TACTICAL. The tactical model of the EOS line is military issue from several governments. Bulletproof and rugged, really waterproof. But the ergonomics are military rough: the button is very hard to push (so it won't wear out), the battery box takes a tool like a dime to open (so they could never fall out by mistake). A better choice if you going to climb mount Everest and your life depends on the lamp. Not as good as this BDSH for using in common outdoor camping, running, hunting, imo.

Those are the two under $50 that I like.

EDIT: I should have noted the reviews stating the tilt lock stops would fail. They failed in 6 months on one of mine of these. The other two I have are getting weaker and weaker (about a year old). Then the lamp just tilts all the way forward and points at your toes. No way to reset the tilt after the mechanism breaks. I changed my rating from 5 stars to 2 stars. I do NOT recommend these.
text_fidelity_b: Black Diamond Spot Headlamp

Dietz #30 Little Wizard Oil Lamp Burning Lantern Blue (Small Tank) Fantastic lantern. If you're used to standard big-box-retailer fare, this lantern is a HUGE step up in quality and size and you'll be very pleasantly surprised. I've burned it ~12 hours and have yet to notice a drop in the fuel level. No smell when burning(except for a few hours after the very first use), even on plain ole kerosene. While it's attractively built and painted, this lantern is clearly built to be used, not just displayed. Packaging was GREAT, I was really surprised at how well this lantern was packaged.

Tips for use: The wick will probably need to be trimmed when you receive it, mine was uneven and had many loose threads. I used angle nippers, a sharp pair of scissors will do better. I just removed the whole burner assembly for easier access and trimmed the wick level with the wick tube. Burn it for several hours the first time OUTSIDE. The paint will be doing it's final outgassing upon being heated and greases and oils from stamping will be burning off during this period, you don't want that going on in your house. When you first light this lantern, turn it up a little bit and let the whole lantern heat up for 10-15 minutes before turning the lantern up to full brightness. Likewise when putting out the lantern, turn it down to a very low flame and let the lantern cool for a few minutes before actually blowing it out. The flame doesn't actually burn liquid fuel, it burns fuel that's vaporized off the wick. If you just blow out the lantern, full throttle to blown out, a bunch of that fuel is still vaporizing off the wick and that smells bad. This can be mitigated considerably by turning down the lantern and letting it cool, which will reduce the amount of fuel that continues to be vaporized after the flame is finally blown out. Odor may be less of an issue with lamp oil, but even with lamp oil, you'll still be inhaling the vaporized lamp oil, even if you're not smelling it. Not healthy.

Now, the one reason I gave 4 stars instead of 5 was that there was a chip down to bare metal on the font when the lantern arrived. As stated above, the packaging was amazing and undamaged, this lantern clearly sustained this chip before being shipped. I used a dab of nailpolish that was fairly close to the color to prevent rust in the future. This did not effect the use of the lantern at all, and I will be buying more.

5/21/16 update: I have several gallons of kerosene through this lantern now. Lantern has performed flawlessly, but I have found that it is actually my least used lantern. It's about the same size, weight, and cost as an Air Pilot, but puts out ~1/2 the light. Yes it burns less fuel, but if you turn down an Air Pilot to the same light level, you'll get about the same fuel consumption while still having the option to turn it up and get more light if you need/want.
text_fidelity_b: Dietz #30 Little Wizard Oil Lamp Burning Lantern Blue (Small Tank)

text_fidelity_a: Brunton 7DNL Baseplate Map Compass I've trekked many miles, guided by the same Brunton 7DNL baseplate compass I received from my wilderness survival camp counselor, decades ago.  There are a few scuffs, and the edges aren't pristine, and yet it still works fine.  It's just as accurate as several $20 ~ $80 compasses my peers carry, and has survived a fair amount of abuse.  While it's not as rugged as some other models, for the price you can buy 2 or 3 of them so you have spares.  As well, you won't feel as guilty should one disappear, or be damaged.  Its compact size makes it handy, but also makes it a little harder to get precise bearings.  It also doesn't have true declination adjustment, only an etched-in scale, which can lead to some issues if you forget this nuance.  For casual trips, I'm quite comfortable with relying on the Brunton 7DNL.  For anything more critical, it's my backup compass (to a more-expensive [[ASIN:B000FEWA6S Suunto M-3DL Compass]], which I tend to baby).

text_fidelity_a:
Gotrax scooter The first shipped scooter came with a snapped off rear fender in a nondescript cardboard box and looked used (sketchy). I contacted amazon and they provided a replacement scooter and a UPS pickup that I now had to worry about missing... Annoying, but whatever.

The second scooter came in COMPLETELY different packaging. Looked legit this time - graphics on the box, in plastic sheeting, etc. Just used the scooter to go about a mile each way (with hills) and it was fine for a 6ft 1in 190lb guy. Did use 1/4 of the battery doing so. The throttle and break levers both stick, so pay attention as it will continue to power even after letting go of the throttle and vise versa for the break. We shall see if it can stand the test of time. I did get the insurance as based off many reviews, this thing is not going to make it long, so I did want to be covered.

You are getting what you pay for here. DO NOT step on the rear fender and I would also not recommend folding, as it snaps onto and stresses the fragile rear (plastic) fender. They also structurally tied the rear foot breaking mechanism into the rear fender as well. Cannot stress enough how not strong and flimsy this rear fender situation is. However for whatever reason, it is an integral part of the functional design of the scooter in many ways. If it snapps off, you are done with the rear foot break.

However for the price, still throwing up 3 stars. Cant expect the world at this price point.
text_fidelity_b: Gotrax scooter

text_fidelity_a:
Freeze Dried Sliced Strawberries by Nutristore | Pack of 2 | Healthy Snack | Emergency Survival Bulk Food Storage | Amazing Taste & Quality | 25 Year Shelf Life These strawberries are beyond delicious! These big #10 (one gallon) cans of freeze dried fruit are IDEAL if you are new to using freeze dried fruits or if you want to put away a couple cans for your family in case of emergency but you don't want to spend $150 on a 6 can case plus shipping from somewhere else. (You simply cannot beat Amazon Prime!)

• • • #10 cans typically hold 12 cups of food and about 11 cups of freeze dried fruits and veggies • • •

It is hard to find information about how much food is actually in a #10 can and have it be accurate enough that you can plan your meals. When filled to the brim with something like rice, the #10 cans hold 12 cups. But freeze dried food is light and not compacted, with air space between the dry pieces so you get about 11 cups (bananas) to 11.25 cups (strawberries and raspberries) in a big can like this. The cans are "full", the difference is simply air space between the fruit pieces. (To be safe, always assume there are 11 cups per #10 can of freeze dried fruits and veggies. I have found this to be accurate and a great way to calculate how much you have stored.)

Now let's talk about how yummy the food is! As I took pictures I could hardly stop my 9 year old son from grabbing handfuls of strawberries behind my back as I tried to snap a quick photo. (The bowl of strawberries was dumped straight into his mouth mere seconds after I got that picture!) The fruit is positively DELICIOUS for snacking straight from the can!

We live in Houston and personally lived through Hurricane Ike in 2008. At the time my son was 18 months old and I would have given anything - ANYTHING - to have these freeze dried strawberries to have offered him. Grocery stores were picked clean the day before the storm. Some of the grocery stores flooded and most of them had damage to roofs, glass doors and building structures from being hit by flung tree branches, fence pieces and debris. We went 12 days without electricity in our home. Grocery stores were without power for the first 5 or 6 days and stayed closed for about a week in our area as they had to be cleaned up before reopening. It was almost 3 weeks after the storm before stores were restocked with fresh produce beyond a few local items like tomatoes and jalapeños. Please, take the advice from someone who has lived through a natural disaster and invest in freeze dried fruits and veggies for your family. Everything in our refrigerators and freezers were ruined by day 2 without power and we still had 10 days to go. The only thing you have to rely on is what you have on your pantry shelves. That is it. These cans will keep for 25 years unopened and truly are a wise investment.

So, since I have been through a natural disaster, I have learned how to bake with freeze dried food since I still live in Houston and may have to deal with another storm in the future. These strawberries did GREAT and I'm going to include the recipe I used so you can have success with them, too. It is wise to open and try the food you are storing but since this company gave several reviewers like myself a discount to test their products, this work has been done for you. You can simply store the cans of food knowing it is superior quality. (I have purchased and used Thrive brand fruits and these taste identical to theirs! In my opinion these strawberries were even better quality.)

• Strawberry Chocolate Chip Muffins •
--> This recipe also works with freeze dried blueberries or other freeze dried fruits
1/4 cup butter, softened
1/3 cup sugar
1 egg, beaten
1/2 cup milk (a small can of evaporated milk is fine to use)
1 cup flour (up to 1.5 cups depending on humidity; batter should be a thick muffin batter)
1 and 1/2 tsp baking powder
1/2 cup freeze dried strawberries (or raspberries or other fruit) rehydrated in 1/2 cup water with the excess liquid drained off
1/2 cup milk chocolate chips

Preheat oven to 400°. Cream butter and sugar. Add the egg and mix well. Add flour alternately with splashes of milk and combine until a thick batter has formed and all ingredients are incorporated. Gently fold in rehydrated fruit. Spoon into 12 paper lined baking cups, filling halfway to 3/4ths full. Bake for 20 minutes or until tops begin to turn golden.

• Tip •
The leftover powder at the bottom of each can is AWESOME for making strawberry butter or adding to oatmeal to make your own fruit and cream flavor. If nothing else, dump the powder in your pancake batter. Don't let the powder go to waste, it is delicious!

Also, if you want to know about the countries of origin on the fruits, this was posted on the seller's FAQ page: "We source our Nutristore foods from some of the following countries: USA, Canada, Ecuador, Greece, Costa Rica, Uruguay, Argentina, Serbia, New Zealand, India, Poland, Mexico & Chile. [We] no longer source foods from China."

I was very fortunate to be able to purchase this pack of freeze dried strawberries at a discount so I could try it, eat it and bake with it before writing a review. I hope that by sharing my photos and experience that you are able to make the best buying decision for your own family! Hugs from Houston!
text_fidelity_b: Freeze Dried Sliced Strawberries by Nutristore | Pack of 2 | Healthy Snack | Emergency Survival Bulk Food Storage | Amazing Taste & Quality | 25 Year Shelf Life

text_fidelity_a:
LaserLyte Laser Sight Center Mass SM Rail The other reviews mentioning the finely threaded battery compartment are pretty accurate. The first thing I did when I got mine was wipe down the threads, there was definitely dust that immediately wiped off that I could see being a problem. After it was cleaned I applied a little bit of mineral oil to the threads (probably something better, but it is what I had), and the screwing/unscrewing was much smoother.

Once I added in the batteries and began screwing the cap back on, I could understand why so many people are worried about it. It is really hard to tell if the resistance you are feeling when screwing it back in is because of the spring on the cap, or because it is not threaded well. If you go carefully it should screw back on fine - especially if you clean the threads and apply a little oil.

The laser seems to function exactly as expected, the strobe mode blinks a little faster than I was expecting, but that is hardly a problem.

Will update once it gets some usage!

UPDATE (2 days later): Well the laser started acting weird... Randomly won't turn on, can't rack a shotgun more than a few times without it turning off - and I wasn't even shooting. I'm actually impressed by just how unreliable it is. Going to roll the dice and get an exchange, but my hopes are not very high at this point.

EDIT: I got a second one of these and am pleased to report that it is more reliable. Was able to put a few dozen rounds thru my shockwave with no issue.

I want to give it 5 stars, but considering the problems so many people have had (myself included) I simply can not.
text_fidelity_b: LaserLyte Laser Sight Center Mass SM Rail

Ideally, honestly we would give them a 4.5/5 star rating if possible due to one flaw (lining up of the lights) but otherwise, they are great and we would both recommend!

Look: We got the black, grey, and blue bands and we both really like the colors. Although the black is standard with FitBit Flex2, the dark blue costs extra, so I really like that we can get all three colors here. One thing I can say about the colors though is that the blue band looks much darker in person than on the photo (although, I actually like it better in real life than on the photo). It's not really a big deal, but I think the different color makes it look just a little more professional and a little less like a typical fitness band. And, since there are three bands, you have choice and can change up your band as you change up your outfits!

Feel: I really like how soft the rubber/silicone material is. It is not stiff (as I have found other after market fitness bands to be), nor is it "sticky" (sometimes rubber can catch fine hairs on the arm and feel like it's ripping them out....that is NOT the case with this band!) The clasp on the back is comfortable and doesn't push into the wrist. Overall, it is very soft and comfortable to wear both during the day and at night.

Fit: there are two aspects here- first how the FitBit Flex2 fits into the band and how the band fits on the wrist. The FitBit fits nicely into the "pouch" left for it- it is secure (does not feel like it will fall out) but is not difficult to get it in either. One of my (only) complaints, however, is that the holes on the bands do not line up PERFECTLY with the lights on the FitBit. Honestly, this is such a minor thing and most people might not even notice it at all. I think it's actually largely because the rubber/silicone is a little bit thicker on this band than it is on the normal band, so it looks a little further away, so depending on your angle when you look at it might look like the entire light isn't on (but I have to say you can always tell which light is on or off, it never covers a light or makes it impossible to see- I think I might be slightly anal retentive to even notice!!). As far as the wrist fit goes...I'm actually really impressed here. It fit my husband without a problem and it even fit my (super dainty) wrists in the second to smallest hole! I feel comfortable to say that this would fit (almost) any adult's wrist. There's no need to keep multiple bands around- one size will definitely fit all.

Security and Protection: Although I have never (ever) worried that the clasp on my Fitbit will wear down and I might eventually lose my FitBit, I can see how that might happen (particularly after long periods of wear and removal to charge). Either way, this band removes any slight concern about that fact with the steel (watch like) clasp. It is obvious this clasp will not accidentally loosen and fall off. Ever. I also like that it feels soft and like it will protect my FitBit in case I (inevitably) bang it into something. The band provides enough protection that I won't break it. That being said, one difference between these bands and the band that comes with is the holes (to view the lights) are open on these bands whereas the are covered with a piece of clear plastic on the regular band it comes with. I'm not sure how much protection that clear plastic provides (I tend to find dust and things on the FitBit regardless), but something to mention.

Overall: I would definitely recommend these bands. I think they're high quality- they look and feel really nice on the wrist. And for the price (3 for ~$10) you really cannot lose.
text_fidelity_b: Usitek Fitbit Flex 2 Accessory Bands for Fitbit Flex 2 / Fitbit Flex2,Silicone Fitness Replacement Accessories Wrist Band for 2016 New Fitbit Flex 2 with Steel Buckle,Pack of 3.

That's just an extra that makes it nicer than having to find a duffel-bag or some other place to carry the set.

It comes with 4 paddles that are the same except for the colors. It has 3 indoor and 3 outdoor balls which are almost identical except for the spacing of the holes. They're like Whiffle™ balls. The holes prevent them from going too far from the air resistance. The ones for indoors are the ones with the bigger holes because you can't hit them as far.

I know it says that you can play indoors and technically that's true, but it depends on where you're playing. A big game room with lots of space would work. A place where you can trip over furniture or knock over lamps isn't a good idea. It also depends on how aggressive you want to be with your swings. The indoor balls are not the problem because they couldn't easily build up enough momentum to break anything except very delicate or top-heavy things. But the paddles swinging around are more of the issue with playing indoors. A big swing or stretch if you aren't aware of the stuff around you could be where you'd break something or trip over something. But still, about the same level of caution you'd have with Ping-Pong, but without the table to keep you in place.

The paddles are pretty nice quality and lighter than they look like they should be. But they have a lot of surface area and the balls are easier to hit than with Ping-Pong paddles.

You'll have to look up the rules online because they aren't included, but really that's only if you want to play "official Pickle-ball". You can play it with Ping-pong rules, badminton rules, volleyball rules, tennis rules -- just about any of the similar kind of games that I can think of -- it's just a bit easier and has requires less skill or movement. It's really about the same level of activity that you'd have with badminton and the same sized area if you're playing outdoors.

Personally, indoors is just if we want to play "hit-the-ball-back-and-forth-down-the-hallway" because it's too hot/cold/wet outside.

This doesn't come with a net, and I thought the rubberband strips might have been to map out the court area, but it's supposed to be for the grip on the paddles. If you're going to play "official" you'll need a net which is pretty much the same as a badminton net just not as high. It's basically a mini tennis court with much the same net.

It's good exercise, and I can't imagine this being a competitive sport, but I was wrong about tag being an 'official' sport when I heard someone mention it -- but it actually is and surprisingly fun to watch -- with sponsors and everything. Pickleball might be the same because why wouldn't someone take something that's fun and add a bunch of rules so they can make some money from advertising.

It's good for staying active and just about everyone likes to play because we don't play with any real rules. Not because we have odd ideas like "there are no losers here", but because it's just that unimportant.

I can't comment on the price with the way things are these days, but it seems to be about the same price as other options, and the quality is decent. The bag is a bonus and even the dog likes to play -- but that's where it goes from being 'pickle-ball' to 'slobber-ball'.

Overall, this is a nice set, especially the paddles. Five stars.
text_fidelity_b: Graphite Pickleball Paddles Set of 4, 2023 USAPA Approved, Carbon Fiber Surface (CHS), Polypropylene Lightweight Honeycomb Core, 3 Indoor 3 Outdoor Pickleball, 4 Replacement Soft Grip + Bag

One shows the actual steps to salsa, merengue, etc. This shows you how to do them, some of their variations, and a quick run through to some music. This is a purely instructional cd. Ignore Joy, pay attention to Beto. I'm not sure why she's there.
The next cd is the Cardio. This will start you out with a warm up routine and then into some dance routines using the above steps you learned. Ignore Joy and watch Beto. I always do the cardio and then decide how much dance I want to do. I might do this 2 or 3 times a day.
And the 3rd cd is the toning cd that includes using the very lightweight toning sticks. They sound a bit like maracas. You don't have to use these, just do the workout routine without them.
Remember, this is for those of us who prefer a slower pace, but it still gets the heart rate up and counts as exercise. Don't complain if you were expecting wild and crazy; this is not that.

text_fidelity_a: Nalgene Tritan Narrow Mouth BPA-Free Water Bottle, Orange w/Blue Cap, 32 oz I always thought these were for city types who spend $1000 on camping gear to spend a weekend in a cabin. Every weekend they invade my small Minnesota town looking for adventure. They've always got the trendy gear and apparel. Most of it is overpriced silliness. I assumed these were the same thing. Boy was I wrong, they are really onto something with these. How can a plastic bottle be so fantastic? First, it's indestructible. I'm pretty sure you could drop one of these from low Earth orbit and it would still be fine when it hit the ground. They don't even get scratched up. I've had one of these bouncing around in the cab of a dump truck for years and it is barely showing wear. These things could be eternal. Second, and most importantly, they NEVER TASTE LIKE SOAP OR PLASTIC! This is my biggest gripe about plastic containers. No mater how much you use them or rinse them, you always taste plastic and you can't get the soap out. These clean and taste like glass. Awesome and worth the $10-12 because they'll outlast anything else

This is in case you are lost or feel for your safety.". Far too often established campgrounds are most with the sounds of people's generators, children, animals, music, etc. A scream for help would be as useless as a whisper. A whistle has the ability to be heard over long distances and other man-made and natural noises.

Three blasts from a whistle is the same as an SOS. People, especially emergency and first responders are trained to respond to SOS whistles. These are not toys.

text_fidelity_a:
GERBER Folding Spade w/Sheath - Model 5940 The Gerber folding shovel is really top notch. Its quality construction is much like any other Gerber/Fiskars equipment I've owned - it doesn't disappoint.

The shovel I have is actually a little more agressively pointed than in the pictures, so I'm not sure if Gerber has addressed this as an issue or if the pictures were off.

The top of the handle is high density polycarbonate plastic and has a horizontal design like a spade should have. You can still use the verticle part of the steel handle if you wish, but there isn't much of it. The plastic will absorb some shock compared to steel-only, and it won't freeze to your hands, etc. The polycarb handle folds down on itself, so that it actually has 3 segments (instead of several designs which have 2 segments). This means you can stow the shovel in the included cordura nylon belt pouch which is no bigger than the shovel head itself. The handle pivot point locks and since it's square, doesn't rotate or twist easily. The steel which connects the blade to the handle fits nicely inside the A angle cutout of the handle, so when collapsed it is really thin.

The blade is high quality steel with the hinged handle connected at the top. This does limit the depth of the shovel a little, but I don't believe it's much of a factor, except maybe in really solid soil where you lose a little verticle travel when the ground butts up against the hinge.

It's very compact, light, comes with a solid belt sheath (easily convertible to pack carry) and stows away easily since it's so thin. I can put it in the side pockets of my doors or in the very small space above my rear wheel well without any problems (Trailblazer 4x4).

I really can find no fault with this item, it delivers on all fronts: usability, quality, compact storage, and rugged design. I will almost certainly be keeping one in both cars and in my 72 Hour survival kit. They are even reasonably priced. 5 Stars.
text_fidelity_b: GERBER Folding Spade w/Sheath - Model 5940

Planet Bike Beamer 3 Bike Headlight This light has two practical safety functions:

It helps make your presence on the road more apparent to on coming traffic. The light is bright enough from even a few hundred feet that a driver would have to be extremely oblivious and distracted not to see it.

Perhaps more importantly, the light will illuminate street signs and signals that are made with a reflective material at distances of over 450 feet away (I measured using google maps). When I first used the light (in flashing mode), I was genuinely shocked to see how the street signs up to two blocks ahead of me were pulsating. I say that this is important because it helps you spot stop signs in the distance - assuming you're being a safe cyclist, biking in a lane, with traffic, abiding by traffic laws, you're probably most likely to get killed by accidently running a stop sign. When I bike home from work at night, I take streets that have no traffic lights and only stop signs, so being able to spot them is very important for me.

The light attaches to your handle bar through via a mount; the light can easily slid off the mount so you don't have to bike around with it during the day, nor leave it on the bike when it's parked outside.

The light does what it needs to do for a reasonable price. I wouldn't hesitate to recommend it.

(My flat sheet was just long enough to tuck under the whole bed, but since the bed is >2' high when inflated, that may have been luck.)

But it doesn't matter how fabulous the features are. If it completely deflates after only a few nights of use, it's a bad bed.I returned it. Guess I'll stick with AeroBed.
text_fidelity_b: WonderSleep Classic Series Air Mattress with DreamCoil Supporting Technology & Internal High Capacity Pump, Air Bed Height 20" - Queen

Zacro Bike Seat Cushion - Gel Padded Bike Seat Cover for Men Women Comfort, Extra Soft Exercise Bicycle Seat Compatible with Peloton, Outdoor & Indoor I'm REALLY pleased with this gel seat cover! I saw an ad for it in some local online newspaper, followed the link to Amazon, and checked it out! Reviews seemed fine, so I sprang for it. It's as good as it looks! Really thick gel that's the perfect cushion for my ROCK HARD bike seat. It appears very well made and comes with a "rain hat" to cover it.

I've comandeered my mountain bike to use as an exerbike during the pandemic year. I put that bike on a Wahoo KICKR, hooked it up to FulGaz virtual rides, pulled on my padded Pearl Izumi bike shorts and..... got EXCRUTIATING sciatica down my right leg for several weeks! I think it's cuz my ROCK HARD bike seat was killing that nerve as I ground away the miles. There's no other exercise I've done that would cause the sciatica. Once I got that painful issue under control with physical therapy, I got right back on the exerbike - but riding on this Zacro gel seat!

All I did is set the gel seat on top of my old bike seat and tie the straps it comes with in a square knot under the front end of my old bike seat; the back of the gel seat secures with a very effective drawstring to hold it snugly to the old bike seat. Took no more than 30 seconds to put it on! The seat does NOT wiggle, slide or shift out of position in a good 10-mi (50 min) ride. I have not had a single sciatica incident since using this gel seat, so I'm HOPING that took care of the problem.

Highly recommend this very practical, well-made gel seat cover for anyone who lacks padding where it counts and wants a comfortable ride.
